K1006/K1018 helped identify normalization and low-dimensional scope; I overextended K1061, whose plain-more-LN condition excludes equal-LN A versus D. C’s attenuation of initial random logits versus E’s preserved signal is a plausible CE explanation, not established evidence. History supplied one comparable low-dimensional normalized comparison: plain won. Lab supplied no low-dimensional low-Δ matched comparisons; two high-dimensional Adagrad comparisons favored plain, whereas four higher-Δ adaptive comparisons favored residual smooth networks. Broader zero-LN low-Δ comparisons split 3/6. These checks do not support a general rule predicting both inversions.

class MLPBlock(nn.Module):
    """One hidden layer: leaky_relu(x + Linear(norm(x)))."""

    def __init__(self, width: int, use_layer_norm: bool) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(width) if use_layer_norm else nn.Identity()
        self.linear = nn.Linear(width, width)
        self.act = nn.LeakyReLU(0.01)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        h = self.linear(self.norm(x))
        h = h + x
        return self.act(h)


class Model(nn.Module):

        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(8, 48),

            MLPBlock(width=48, use_layer_norm=True),
            MLPBlock(width=48, use_layer_norm=True),
            MLPBlock(width=48, use_layer_norm=True),
            MLPBlock(width=48, use_layer_norm=False),
            nn.Linear(48, 2),
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.net(x)

def loss_fn(model: nn.Module, pred: torch.Tensor, target: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:

        return torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(pred.reshape(-1, vocab), target.reshape(-1))
